title: Democrats are running on a scant agenda. Do they need more?
description: They lack a specific plan for governing, beyond turning back Trump and holding him accountable.

title: Arizona’s GOP keeps embracing election deniers who lose. It could happen again.
description: Alexander Kolodin made his political career by championing challenges to the 2020 results. Now he’s running to lead his state’s elections.

title: These are the voters who will decide the midterm elections
description: Move aside, “soccer moms.” Take our quiz to see which types of Americans will determine control of Congress in November.

title: 35 years ago today, Anita Hill testified before Congress
description: Hill’s testimony was a watershed in the conversation about workplace sexual harassment. The Almanac uses photo archives to understand where we are by examining where we’ve been.

title: Politics chat: Trump announces fuel deal with Russia. What does it mean for sanctions?
description: President Trump announced a deal to import Russian fuel to the U.S. We look at what this means for the sanctions he recently signed off on against Russia, as well as the U.S.'s support for Ukraine.

title: Reshaped civil rights mission at Justice Department transforms its work, workforce
description: Harmeet Dhillon has pushed out hundreds of longtime attorneys, replaced many with inexperienced ideological allies, and used the division's enforcement powers to pursue the president's agenda.

title: In one of the country's most competitive districts, a Democrat tries to keep her seat
description: In a highly competitive Washington congressional race, the incumbent Democrat has angered part of her party base and the Trump-backed Republican challenger faces backlash against the party in power.

title: DOJ investigating five TV networks over White House pool coverage
description: The agency said the probe seeks to determine whether Fox News, CNN, ABC, CBS and NBC violated antitrust laws. It marks a sharp escalation in the Trump administration’s use of its powers against perceived enemies in the press.

title: Trump suggests ‘Ocean of Americas’ as new name for Atlantic or Pacific
description: The president also floated the idea of naming an ocean after himself.

title: Trump says Ukraine should ‘get a new president’ after U.S.-Russia diesel deal
description: Ukraine’s Zelensky "wants to make problems for the world," Trump said Saturday, a day after praising Russia’s Putin.

title: Trump's economic strategy resemble similar policies in East Asia
description: Much of the Trump administration's economic policy has been inspired by successful industrial policies successful in East Asia, including those of competitor, China. Will those policies work in the U.S.?

title: Trump says he will ‘make a decision’ on Hegseth plan to live-stream execution
description: The Pentagon has said a firing squad for the Fort Hood shooter is scheduled for Dec. 3. “By showing it, maybe other people won’t be doing what he did,” the president said.

title: Christa Pike discharged from hospital, 10 days after failed execution
description: Pike, who survived an execution attempt in Tennessee, has been moved to a rehabilitation center, according to her attorneys and the Tennessee Department of Correction.

title: Trump fumes at ‘stain’ on Norway after missing out on Nobel Peace Prize
description: The president described the decision to award the Nobel Peace Prize to Navi Pillay as “disgraceful and embarrassing” and said he would “not forget.”

title: Montana Democrat who refuses to drop out may spoil party’s Senate hopes
description: Candidate Alani Bankhead vigorously denies claims she is a Republican plant running to take votes away from a more popular independent.

title: Darline Graham opposes Chinese manufacturing. Her husband’s job relies on it.
description: The senator and sister of the late Lindsey Graham has said the U.S. must “stop depending on Communist China for things America can make ourselves.”

title: These lawmakers want to head off a potential post-election crisis
description: A bipartisan effort is underway in Congress to avert a constitutional crisis, where Republicans don't seat Democrats, if they win the chamber.

title: Why former Republican governors are backing a Democrat for Senate in a red state
description: Adam Hamilton, the Democratic Senate candidate in Kansas, is running as a centrist rather than a hyper-partisan and needs Republican votes to win the race.

title: U.S. imposes sweeping sanctions on International Criminal Court
description: The U.S. has announced sanctions against the International Criminal Court, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio vowing to dismantle the world's only permanent war crimes tribunal.

title: Week in Politics: Hegseth's livestream backlash; Greece ambassador Guilfoyle scandal
description: Bipartisan blowback on Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's plans to livestream a military execution, plus a scandal involving Kimberly Guilfoyle, the US Ambassador to Greece.

title: On the ground in Ohio's 9th District: The battleground shaping next month's midterms
description: Ohio is a critical battleground in next month's midterms elections. NPR's Scott Simon traveled to the state's 9th Congressional District to hear from voters about their priorities.

title: After losing ground with Latino voters, Democrats are turning to influencers for help
description: Democrats are hoping to win back Latino voters who have soured on both parties. They hope Latino content creators will bridge the gap.

title: The midterms are getting close. Why is Trump in Upstate New York?
description: Trump bet that his presence could turn out conservative Republicans in the gubernatorial race. But even some in the MAGA base aren’t confident about the odds.

title: Texas Senate nominee James Talarico reappears after multi-day absence
description: The Democrat’s campaign said he was recovering from the flu, while Republicans tried to make his absence seem suspicious.

title: D.C. judge bars DOJ from gathering states’ voter lists to find noncitizens
description: Voting rights groups had challenged the effort, noting federal data includes errors that have led to citizens being wrongly removed from electoral rolls.

title: Trump announces diesel deal with Russia in bid to lower prices
description: The amount is small compared with U.S. demand, but the deal aligns the U.S. with Russia and against Ukraine’s efforts to bomb Russian refineries.

title: Trump taps conservative commentator as next White House press secretary
description: Katie Zacharia replaces Karoline Leavitt, who departed the White House in August after giving birth to her second child.

title: Ocasio-Cortez will stump for Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan’s Senate race
description: The matchup will test the strength of the Democratic Party’s progressive wing — and the congresswoman’s potential 2028 chances — in a battleground state.

title: Democratic women’s caucus demands Trump administration changes after Cornell accusations
description: The lawmakers said the case “raised questions about the Title IX process and discipline imposed by Cornell University.”

title: Cook moves 18 more House races toward the left
description: Polling and the work of prognosticators like the Cook Political Report suggest Democrats are likely to take back the House in November.

title: Trump says U.S. to get diesel from Russia, relaxing pressure on Moscow to ease prices before midterms
description: Trump says the U.S. will obtain diesel from Russia, relaxing years of U.S. pressure on Moscow, to combat prices before midterms. He said he struck the deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin in a phone call.

title: Trump is trying last-minute ways to bring down prices
description: What happened under the Trump administration this week that you may have missed.

title: Trump escalates effort to fire Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook
description: A commission that will report to the president will assess the mortgage fraud allegations against her and consider evidence from a hearing next month.

title: A Republican attack ad misidentifies its Democratic target. Twice.
description: A GOP ad used a photo of Republican Myron Lizer instead of Democrat Jonathan Nez. Nez is challenging Rep. Eli Crane (R-Arizona).

title: Trump's Affordable Suit
description: NPR's Mary Louise Kelly speaks with New York Times fashion reporter Jacob Gallagher about President Trump's apparent choice to wear a suit from the budget menswear chain Jos. A. Bank.
